application.name: Permit Intake Service
application.scope: One service: the permit intake API and its persistence model. Permit inspection and billing services are out of scope for this run.
application.scope_note: Split larger programs into one run per application or service rather than truncating the rule set.

documentation_sources.title: Permit intake user guide
documentation_sources.note: Last revised two releases before the reviewed commit.

documentation_sources.title: Intake officer training deck
documentation_sources.location: Referenced by the intake team; no copy was available in the repository or supplied for this run.

documentation_gap.summary: The intake officer training deck was referenced but could not be inspected.
documentation_gap.coverage_impact: Rules that exist only in training material cannot be confirmed, so reconciliation coverage is reduced and some rules are recorded as implemented-only rather than aligned.

facets.label: Eligibility
facets.description: Decides whether an applicant may proceed.

facet_groups.label: Rule kind
facet_groups.description: How the rule is enforced in the implementation.

rules.title: Applicants must be 19 or older on the submission date
rules.statement: An intake submission is rejected when the applicant's date of birth places them under 19 years of age on the submission date, evaluated in the America/Vancouver time zone.
rules.rationale: Age of majority governs who may hold a permit in their own name.

match_notes.reason: Blocks submission before any downstream processing.

reconciliation.note: The guide and the validator agree on the threshold and the evaluation date.

rules.title: Base application fee is calculated from permit class and duration
rules.statement: The base fee equals the permit class rate multiplied by the requested duration in months, rounded to the nearest cent using banker's rounding, before any exemption is applied.

reconciliation.note: No available document describes the rounding mode; the training deck that may describe it was unavailable.

rules.title: Only intake officers may reopen a withdrawn application
rules.statement: Reopening a withdrawn application requires the intake-officer role; applicants receive a permission failure and the attempt is recorded in the audit log.

reconciliation.note: The guide states that supervisors may also reopen applications; the implementation checks the intake-officer role only.

rules.title: Withdrawn applications are purged after seven years
rules.statement: Withdrawn applications and their attachments are removed seven years after the withdrawal date.

reconciliation.note: The guide describes the retention period, but no scheduled job, migration, or configuration implementing it was found in this service.

rules.title: Paper submissions receive a manual review queue entry
rules.statement: Paper submissions once created a manual review queue entry before automated validation.

reconciliation.note: The implementation was removed before the reviewed commit; the rule is retained for traceability.

retirement.reason: Paper submissions were discontinued and the queue was deleted.

diagrams.title: Intake decision flow
diagrams.description: Order in which eligibility, authorization, and fee rules are applied to a submission.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[Submission received] --> B{Applicant 19 or older?}
  B -- No --> R[Reject: BR-0001]
  B -- Yes --> C{Role permits action?}
  C -- No --> D[Permission failure: BR-0003]
  C -- Yes --> E[Calculate base fee: BR-0002]
  E --> F[Persist application record]

diagrams.title: Application lifecycle states
diagrams.description: States a permit application moves through, including the retention path.
diagrams.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Draft
  Draft --> Submitted
  Submitted --> Withdrawn
  Submitted --> Approved
  Withdrawn --> Purged: seven years (BR-0004)
  Approved --> [*]

open_questions: Which role list is correct for reopening a withdrawn application (BR-0003)?
Is the seven-year retention rule implemented in another service, or not implemented at all (BR-0004)?
